sections.h2: Brandenburg offices for your tax bill
sections.html:
Nearly everything happens in two suites at 516 Hillcrest Drive. The assessor, formally the Property Valuation Administration (PVA), is in Suite 3 and takes calls at (270) 422-2178 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Sheriff's Office is in Suite 14, where payments are accepted, at (270) 422-4937.

Value is decided in one suite and collected in the other. Walk exemption and value questions into Suite 3. Carry the bill itself to Suite 14. The County Clerk gets involved only after April 15, once unpaid bills have been transferred.

Payment goes to the Sheriff. Bills are mailed each fall, and when mail runs late the Sheriff's office posts an online lookup so owners can check what they owe while the paper bill catches up. The dates below follow KRS 134.015, but the law allows a different schedule when mailing is delayed, so ask the Sheriff which dates apply to your bill.

Meade County payment schedule
When you payEffect on the bill
By November 12 percent discount
Through New Year's EveNo discount, no penalty
January5 percent added
After January10 percent added

The Sheriff stops collecting on April 15, with the window shutting at 4:30 in the afternoon. Personal checks are refused for the last two weeks of each collection season, so late payers need cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check. The office calls this a yearly custom, and personal checks are taken again earlier in the season.

sections.h2: What a typical Meade County house owes
sections.html:
A typical owned home here carries a value of $207,900. The state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents on each $100, and the county, the school district and special districts add their own levies. Owning costs $1,344 a month with a mortgage and $462 without one. A typical renter pays $1,026, and household income is $74,355.

Growth has been steady. The head count climbed from 9,422 in 1950 to 18,938 in 1960 and reached 30,003 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate of 30,699 is 2.3 percent above that. With 165 new-construction permits in 2025, new houses compete with resale listings.

Owners occupy 74.1 percent of homes. In 2020 there were 11,943 housing units, 7.5 percent of them vacant, and tenants lived in 27.2 percent of the occupied ones. A seller with a tenant in place should settle showing access with the tenant before listing.

Owners aged 65 or more, and those who are totally disabled, can have $49,100 shaved off assessed value for 2025 and 2026 under state law. Because it comes off before rates apply, every levy on the bill shrinks with it.

The PVA sets a spring deadline each year for applications to make the November bill. Someone turning 65 soon should call the office to learn the current date. Filing early also helps the taxing districts plan their budgets. Proof of age can be a birth certificate, a driver's license or a passport. Disability claims depend on a finding of total disability and must be renewed annually. Renewal is waived for an owner with a service-connected disability and for anyone Social Security or state retirement has ruled permanently disabled.

Your first step is a conference at the PVA, where staff explain the way your value was built. The state calendar takes over from there:

  • The roll can be viewed for 13 days from the first Monday in May.
  • Hand the appeal to the County Clerk's office by closing time on the next business day.
  • Collect land and building records, such as insurance papers, construction costs and comparable sale listings.
  • Attend the local board of assessment appeals, which convenes roughly a month after viewing for up to five days.

Recording the hearing is allowed. Should the board land above your claim once bills are out, a supplemental bill makes up the difference.

Selling the house doesn't erase the debt. Whatever is open on April 15 becomes a certificate held by the Clerk, who files a lien and starts 1 percent monthly interest. Under KRS 134.420 the lien may last 11 years under any owner.

Two letters come from the county attorney: the first inside 30 days of the transfer, the second inside 60. The Clerk then sets a sale 90 to 135 days out, and a certificate buyer may add substantial fees. Before April 15 the Sheriff quotes the payoff, and after that date the Clerk does. The closing agent settles it out of the sale money.

Get the payoff on paper and make sure it covers every year with a balance, not just the latest bill.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Meade County
sections.html:
Meade County was created in 1823 and covers 325 square miles. The Ohio River forms its 56-mile northern line, facing Indiana. Karst terrain with sinkholes covers much of the land, and the northwest sits on a plateau behind the Dripping Springs Escarpment. Brandenburg is the seat, Ekron and Muldraugh are the other cities, and Doe Valley and Fort Knox are census-designated places. Meade lies in the Louisville metro area, within reach of the job centers at Elizabethtown and Fort Knox, and workers travel a mean 33.0 minutes to their jobs.

Meade County Schools, with Meade County High School, teach most children, while families living on the Fort Knox base are zoned to the Defense Department's schools. The county keeps Eastern time.

Sinkholes are common in this terrain, and a house with one, or with deferred repairs, can stall a conventional sale. Ground conditions vary from one parcel to the next, so a buyer's inspection may ask about them. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can close without those fixes.

Location also shapes demand. Fort Knox and Elizabethtown employers are a short drive away, and the Ohio River frontage faces Indiana, so buyers from the Louisville side often compare Brandenburg listings with those in Hardin County. Priced against the $207,900 median, a well kept house with clear title and a current tax payoff tends to move faster than one with open questions.

Start by phoning the PVA to confirm the parcel record and any homestead claim, then ask the Sheriff for the current bill. If the sale will close after April 15, plan to get the payoff from the County Clerk instead. Expect the title company to ask for both figures, along with a copy of the deed. When the owner has died, bring the papers showing who may sign the deed.

Showings go better when the house is ready for a walk-through, but you aren't required to fix anything for a cash sale. If the sinkhole question comes up, a buyer will want to know what you know about it, so be ready to answer plainly. Keep copies of your tax receipts for recent years. They show the title company the bills were paid and speed up the payoff check. If a tenant lives in the house, tell the buyer early and give the lease terms, since a lease may stay in force after the sale. Finally, ask the Sheriff about payment methods for your closing date, because the personal-check rule near the end of the season can matter if the closing falls close to April 15

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Meade County Sheriff?
faqs.a: Go to 516 Hillcrest Drive, Suite 14, in Brandenburg, or call (270) 422-4937. Suite 3, the PVA, can't accept payments.

faqs.q: When does the Meade County Sheriff stop taking personal checks?
faqs.a: From two weeks before April 15 onward. Cash, cards, money orders and cashier's checks are still accepted.

faqs.q: When is the homestead filing cutoff in Meade County?
faqs.a: The PVA sets a spring date each year for a place on the November bill. Call the office for the current cutoff.

faqs.q: What is the state rate in Meade County?
faqs.a: The state's 2025 rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. County, school and district levies come on top.

faqs.q: What becomes of Meade County bills left open after April 15?
faqs.a: The Clerk receives them as certificates of delinquency and files a lien. Interest accrues at 1 percent monthly, and the Clerk may schedule a sale within 90 to 135 days.
